knowledge_point.title: Finding the Number of Intersection Points of Two Lines

question.:question/problem:
Consider the lines $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$, defined by

$$
\begin{alignedat}{2}
l_{1}:\quad & y &{}={}& 2x - 6 \\[6pt]
l_{2}:\quad & 5x + 5y &{}={}& 15
\end{alignedat}
$$

At how many points do these lines intersect?

The lines $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The number of points of intersection between the two lines is equal to the number of solutions of the corresponding system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y &= 2x - 6 \\ 5x + 5y &= 15\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve the system using substitution. The first equation already gives $y$ in terms of $x$:

$$
y = 2x - 6
$$

Then, we substitute

$$
y=2x - 6
$$

into the second equation and solve for $x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
5x + 5y &= 15 \\
5x + 5\left(2x - 6\right) &= 15 \\
5x + 10x - 30 &= 15 \\
15x - 30 &= 15 \\
15x &= 45
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient of $x$ is nonzero, so this equation determines exactly one value of $x$. The first equation then determines exactly one value of $y$. Therefore, the system has one solution.

Consequently, the lines intersect at one point.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the lines $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$, defined by

$$
\begin{alignedat}{2}
l_{1}:\quad & -2x + y &{}={}& -6 \\[6pt]
l_{2}:\quad & -20x + 4y &{}={}& 8
\end{alignedat}
$$

At how many points do these lines intersect?

The lines $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The number of points of intersection between the two lines is equal to the number of solutions of the corresponding system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x + y &=-6 \\ -20x + 4y &= 8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve the system using substitution. First, we solve for $y$ in the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-2x + y &=-6 \\
y &= 2x - 6
\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute

$$
y=2x - 6
$$

into the second equation and solve for $x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-20x + 4y &= 8 \\
-20x + 4\left(2x - 6\right) &= 8 \\
-20x + 8x - 24 &= 8 \\
-12x - 24 &= 8 \\
-12x &= 32
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient of $x$ is nonzero, so this equation determines exactly one value of $x$. The first equation then determines exactly one value of $y$. Therefore, the system has one solution.

Consequently, the lines intersect at one point.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the lines $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$, defined by

$$
\begin{alignedat}{2}
l_{1}:\quad & 3x - 2y &{}={}& -6 \\[6pt]
l_{2}:\quad & -8x - 12y &{}={}& 1
\end{alignedat}
$$

At how many points do these lines intersect?

The lines $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The number of points of intersection between the two lines is equal to the number of solutions of the corresponding system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x - 2y &=-6 \\ -8x - 12y &= 1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve the system using substitution. First, we solve for $y$ in the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}
3x - 2y &=-6 \\
-2y &= -3x - 6 \\
y &= \frac{-3x - 6}{-2} \\
y &= \frac{3}{2}x + 3
\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute

$$
y=\frac{3}{2}x + 3
$$

into the second equation and solve for $x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-8x - 12y &= 1 \\
-8x - 12\left(\frac{3}{2}x + 3\right) &= 1 \\
-8x - 18x - 36 &= 1 \\
-26x - 36 &= 1 \\
-26x &= 37
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient of $x$ is nonzero, so this equation determines exactly one value of $x$. The first equation then determines exactly one value of $y$. Therefore, the system has one solution.

Consequently, the lines intersect at one point.
